findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_chains, how_to_get_api_key, rpc_call, data_api_get, get_account · Private data: search_docs, estimate_usage, how_to_get_api_key, list_docs, rpc_call, data_api_get, get_account, get_deposit_address · Public sink: list_docs, send_raw_transaction · Destructive: rpc_call.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_chains, how_to_get_api_key, rpc_call, data_api_get, get_account · Private data: search_docs, estimate_usage, how_to_get_api_key, list_docs, rpc_call, data_api_get, get_account, get_deposit_address · Public sink: list_docs, send_raw_transaction · Destructive: rpc_call

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_docs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Search documentation pages using keywords against page title, relative path, and first-paragraph summary. Returns matching page titles, paths, and summaries." → after: "Find documentation by topic or task keywords when the page path is unknown. Searches page titles, navigation titles, relative paths, and page summaries, returning titles, relative paths, and summaries. Read a result with read_doc using its path and the same lang; use read_doc directly for a known pa"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
